Population.evidence_source: [/page/4/Text/12] Several of their children described how this nonexpression of feelings had made them feel that they 'didn't know' their father/mother.

Area.evidence_source: [/page/4/Text/8] The informants described the elderly as having little ability to open up or to convey their feelings to those around them. [/page/4/Text/10] One daughter described her father as "disciplined" – her father was of the opinion that one should keep one's troubles to oneself. "He never mentioned his problems," she said. [/page/4/Text/11] The informants said that these traits had made it difficult to help the elderly. One daughter said, "Nobody realized he was ill. He's always been like that – gritted his teeth, pulled himself together."
